identity.title: Revisiting the Extended Schmidt Law: The Important Role of Existing Stars in Regulating Star Formation

paper_type_evidence.loc: 3 An updated version of the extended Schmidt law
paper_type_evidence.quote: individual star formation regions in LIRGs NGC 1614 and IC 4687 as observed by ALMA
We revisit the proposed extended Schmidt law (Shi et al. 2011) which points that the star formation efficiency in galaxies depends on the stellar mass surface density

question.value: Does the extended Schmidt law (SFR depending on gas and stellar mass surface density) hold across a wide range of environments, including outer disks of dwarfs, spirals, mergers, GMCs and high-z galaxies?

evidence.quote:
We find that these regions are distributed in a tight power-law as $\Sigma_{\rm       SFR}{\propto} ({\Sigma_{\rm
      star}^{0.5}}{\Sigma_{\rm  gas}})^{1.09}$
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00182.S.
The total gas mass is measured based on the CO 6-5 map as observed by ALMA
the gas mass is based on CO J=2-1 emission as observed by ALMA
as observed by ALMA (cite: Xu15) with a synthesized beam of 0.26$\times$0.20 arcsec$^{2}$

analysis_steps.goal: NGC 1614 gas surface density from ALMA CO 6-5

method.value: Integrate CO 6-5 over 4500-5000 km/s, convert to Sigma_gas via 13.5 x f_CO(6-5)

evidence.quote: $\Sigma_{\rm gas} = 13.5{\times}f_{\rm CO(6-5)},$
CO 6-5 is first converted to CO 2-1 by assuming a brightness temperature ratio of 0.72 between the two

assumptions.value: X_CO = 2e20 cm^-2 with factor 1.36 for helium

evidence.quote: then used the conversion factor $X_{\rm  CO}$ = 2$\times$10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$ for CO 1-0 with an additional factor of 1.36 for the helium

analysis_steps.goal: Fit the extended Schmidt law to all regions

method.value: Best-fit power law of SFR, gas and stellar surface densities; medians and scatter with bootstrap errors

evidence.quote: The associated error bars were derived based on the bootstrap.
\Sigma_{\rm SFR} = 10^{-4.76}(\Sigma_{\rm star}^{0.5}\Sigma_{\rm gas})^{1.09}
The 1-$\sigma$ apparent scatter of the relationship is about 0.30 dex.

results_numeric.quantity: Median offset of metal-poor regions, KS to extended Schmidt

evidence.quote: with the median offset dropping from a factor of 60 in the Kennicutt-Schmidt plane to a factor of 9 in the extended Schmidt plane

results_numeric.quantity: Dwarf outer-disk median offset, extended Schmidt

findings_qualitative.value: Mid-plane pressure is well approximated by Sigma_star^0.5 Sigma_gas, supporting a role for stellar gravity.

evidence.quote:
the mid-plane pressure is well approximated by the term ${\Sigma_{\rm
    star}^{0.5}}{\Sigma_{\rm  star}}$

claims.hypothesis: Stellar mass surface density regulates star formation in addition to gas.
claims.experiment: Compiled SFR, gas and stellar mass surface densities for regions in dwarfs, spirals, LIRGs, M33 GMCs and high-z galaxies and fit the extended Schmidt law.
claims.result: Single power law with slope 1.09 and 0.30 dex scatter.
claims.finding: Extended Schmidt law holds across environments.

evidence.quote: These results suggest an important role for existing stars in helping to regulate star formation through the effect of their gravity on the mid-plane pressure

claims.hypothesis: Outer disks of dwarfs follow the extended Schmidt law while deviating from KS and Silk-Elmegreen.
claims.experiment: Measured 114 regions in three dwarf galaxies and computed offsets.
claims.finding: Dwarf outer disks follow the extended Schmidt law with large scatter.

limitations_admitted.value: Same X_CO adopted for all sources for simplicity; smaller values for starbursts would steepen the slopes.

evidence.quote: As a result, we used the same factor for simplicity.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA data are a small part of the sample; the result depends on heterogeneous SFR and mass tracers.
Uniform X_CO and a fixed stellar mass-to-light ratio may bias slopes.
